title: Version pin interaction with autoscaler caused rollback to fail during high-traffic rollout
text:
Version pin interaction with autoscaler caused rollback to fail during high-traffic rollout

description:
During a canary-to-production rollout of model v3.1, an unexpected interaction between version pinning and the autoscaler prevented the rollback path from completing. Traffic surged due to an external spike in requests; autoscaler scaled new pods but pinned instances prevented the fleet leader from accepting fallback routing, leaving ~18% of requests served by a misconfigured variant for 23 minutes. This produced a measurable uptick in latency and error rates for a subset of customers and triggered elevated support tickets.

timeline:
2026-03-01T10:05Z - Canary rollout for v3.1 started (scheduled canary 5% traffic)
2026-03-01T10:17Z - External traffic spike begins from large partner integration (traffic x4 baseline)
2026-03-01T10:20Z - Monitoring alert: per-route p50/p95 latency increased; error rate to 3.8%
2026-03-01T10:28Z - Automatic rollback triggered by SLO guardrails (error rate threshold exceeded)
2026-03-01T10:29Z - Rollback job attempted but encountered pinned version lock on 2 leader nodes
2026-03-01T10:32Z - Ops manually attempted immediate rollback, but controllers deferred due to pin metadata mismatch
2026-03-01T10:45Z - Partial mitigation: traffic rerouted to second region for affected customer subset
2026-03-01T10:58Z - Cleanup script executed to clear stale pin metadata; rollback completed by 10:58Z
2026-03-01T11:30Z - Post-incident monitoring: error rates returned to baseline; incident declared mitigated

detection:
Automated SLO guardrails and per-route latency/error thresholds triggered the initial alert. On-call noticed rollback did not reduce error rate as expected and escalated to runtime on-call.

root_cause:
A sequence of events: (1) customer-triggered traffic spike exposed a race between autoscaler scale-up and rollout controller. (2) Two nodes retained a version pin flag from a prior manual pin operation; rollout controller's safety checks skipped rollback for pinned nodes. (3) The fallback routing logic expected immediate node-level acceptance but encountered inconsistent pin metadata leading to a partially applied rollback state. Lack of end-to-end validation of pin state across controllers allowed the partially-applied state to persist until manual cleanup.

mitigations:
Immediate: manual metadata cleanup and forced unpin script executed to unblock rollback (ops runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6124)
Short-term: add a post-rollback validation step that asserts routing weights and pin states are consistent across all leader nodes (hotfix merged: runtime-1.23.1)
Medium-term: enhance rollout controller to treat stale pin metadata as ignorable if newer rollout epoch supersedes it (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RO/Pin-Policy-Design)
Medium-term: autoscaler/rollout coordination — add ‘scale-consensus’ barrier to ensure controllers observe stabilized node set before applying pin-sensitive actions
Long-term: add system test that simulates concurrent traffic spikes + pinned nodes to catch regressions in CI (playbook in QA repo)
Observability: add Grafana panel that surfaces pin state divergence and a Grafana alert for >0.5% nodes with inconsistent pin state: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/rollout-health?orgId=1&var-rollout=ENG-35820

action_items:
ENG-35821 - Implement forced-unpin fallback in rollout controller (owner: Miguel Ortega, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-35822 - Add post-rollback validation and automatic reconciliation job (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-35823 - Implement scale-consensus barrier between autoscaler and rollout controller (owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, due: 2026-04-02)
ENG-35824 - Add CI system test for pin+spike scenarios and include in canary gate (owner: QA Team, due: 2026-03-29)
OPS-2026 - Update runbook with explicit manual-unpin steps and add automation to detect stale pins during incident detection (owner: Jordan Blake, due: 2026-03-15)
SRE-440 - Create Grafana alert and dashboard tile for pin divergence and attach to on-call escalation (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2026-03-12)
PM-118 - Customer communication follow-up and post-incident report to affected customers with incident timeline and mitigations (owner: Lina Fernández, due: 2026-03-14)

postmortem_notes:
We did not have a clear ownership boundary for node pin metadata lifecycle; this allowed manual operations to leave residual state that rollout controller did not reconcile.
The autoscaler assumes idempotent node additions; rollout controller assumes pin state is authoritative. We need a canonical source-of-truth and reconciliation loop.
Incident revealed a gap in our e2e testing: concurrent scale + rollout operations are not covered by existing CI scenarios.
Customer-impact mapping: 14 enterprise customers experienced transient latency increases; one partner integration saw timeouts requiring support intervention. No data loss.
Communication: initial status updates were sent within 30 minutes; follow-up customer notes will include technical detail and mitigation steps. Support tickets linked in case notes.

follow_up_notes:
Evaluate whether version pin feature should be gated behind RBAC and audit events to avoid accidental manual pins.
Discuss adding a TTL to manual pins so they cannot persist indefinitely without review.
Consider a small engineering investment to surface pin ownership and last-modified actor in the Console rollout view.
Cross-team retro scheduled 2026-03-15 with SRE, Runtime, Autoscale, and PM to align on ownership and timeline for action items.
